speaker: Remy
practice: Write a skill as an SOP, not as prose advice: fixed modes, explicit field schemas, and a stated extraction discipline, so output stays comparable across sessions instead of drifting.
rationale: An underspecified skill re-invents its own format each run, which destroys any cross-session comparison built on top of it.
effect_test: Claims per 1,000 words stays inside a stable band per source type across future ingests. Baseline set 2026-08-25 over 19 sources: youtube median 1.27/1k (range 0.71-4.25), newsletter median 2.82/1k (range 2.38-5.62). A >2x drift in either band means the SOP is not holding.
effect_note: Baseline recorded. Written sources run ~2.2x denser than spoken, which is structural (edited argument vs. conversation), not extractor drift - compare within type only.
quote: skills are literally just SOPs for AI.

speaker: Remy
practice: Keep skills in a GitHub repository published as a plugin, rather than as loose files on one machine, so there is one source of truth with version history.
rationale: Skills that live on individual machines cannot be versioned, shared, or rolled back; the repo makes the workflow an asset rather than a local habit.
effect_test: Retired without passing. The test was: installing from a GitHub URL on a second machine yields the same skill, and a commit on one machine reaches the other. Never ran - the repo was never pushed and the plugin path had no update mechanism.
effect_note: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-27. The plugin route was abandoned and its artifacts deleted (_tools\signal-kb.plugin and _tools\signal-kb-plugin\ removed by Jim 2026-08-27; plugins/synced is empty and no signal-kb registration survives outside .trash). Reason: the .plugin upload path is install-only - it rejected v0.3.1 with 'a plugin named signal-kb is already installed' and offers no update path - so it actively PREVENTED the single source of truth this practice exists to create. The GitHub repo half was never pushed, so the version history it promised was never delivered. Function split on retirement: the backup, rollback and integrity-verification half moved to prac-005 (dated Drive snapshots with SHA-256 manifest, effect test passed), and the skill now syncs to Jim's account directly - the saved signal-kb SKILL.md was verified byte-identical to the delivered file on 2026-08-27, which is the one-source-of-truth outcome the plugin failed to produce. **GAP THIS LEAVES, stated plainly:** nothing now carries the skill AND the PowerShell fetchers to a second machine as one installable unit. The skill syncs; _tools\Get-Transcripts.ps1, Get-Written.ps1, Install-Deno.ps1, yt-dlp.exe and the .bat launchers do not, and must be copied from Drive by hand. That is an accepted cost, not a solved problem. Reopen this practice if a plugin update path ever ships, or if a second machine actually needs the pipeline.
quote: The best way that I've found is by putting them all in a GitHub repository and making it a plug-in.

speaker: Remy
practice: Append a self-improvement pass to the end of the skill: after every run, ask what failed, what the user corrected, and what a future run would need - and log it rather than acting on it immediately.
rationale: Failures are visible only at the moment they happen; without a logging step they are re-discovered every session.
effect_test: At least one SKILL.md change traces to the three-occurrence rule in schema-notes.md rather than to an ad-hoc edit, and schema-notes.md keeps accumulating entries that the next run acts on.
effect_note: PASSED once. Quote elision was logged three times (7/71, 2/21, 2/43 failures) before Mode 4 verification was made mandatory and the no-ellipsis rule was written into SKILL.md. Three further patterns are mid-count: chronological novelty (1), date precision (2), event grouping (2), cross-file quote attribution (1).
quote: did any step fail or need a workaround.

speaker: Remy
practice: Split a process into a chain of separate skills whenever a sub-process will ever need to run on its own, rather than writing one skill that does everything.
rationale: A monolithic skill forces the whole pipeline to run to reach any one step, and makes the unused steps' instructions compete for attention.
effect_test: If adopted: a query-only or scoring-only run stops loading the ingest and extraction instructions it does not use.
effect_note: NOT adopted. The fetchers are already a chain (Get-Transcripts / Get-Written), but Modes 1-6 remain one file. Splitting is premature: the modes share the schema definitions, and duplicating those across files is exactly the drift prac-001 exists to prevent. Revisit if SKILL.md exceeds roughly twice its current length.
quote: you can pretty much automate any process within a company as long as it's not physical like washing dishes.

speaker: Remy
practice: Back up skills to version control on the cloud. A skill library is hours of accumulated work living as a single mutable copy in one directory that an agent can delete.
rationale: Remy lost a Claude folder holding 150 skills and 500+ hours of work when Claude deleted it, with no backups. The loss mode is not hardware failure - it is the agent itself, operating on the directory it reads from.
effect_test: A deliberate deletion of a saved skill can be restored from the newest dated snapshot and verified byte-identical against INVENTORY.csv, and a new dated folder appears in Skills-Backup on the 1st of each month.
effect_note: ADOPTED 2026-08-25 and the effect test has ALREADY PASSED once. First snapshot written to Google Drive AI\Skills-Backup\2026-08-25 (13 skills, 216 files; authored set 388,484 bytes across 9 skills). Round-trip verified by staging the archive back OUT of Drive and unzipping it: all 9 authored SKILL.md files byte-identical to the live skills, all 9 SHA-256 content hashes and file counts matched INVENTORY.csv, and the restored signal-kb SKILL.md passed validate-skill.py. Monthly task trig_01Gyv7PbVEKUwhwqcDV1HDFo runs 1st at 13:00 UTC, writes via the Google Drive connector so it does not need Jim's computer awake, and has push and email notifications on. KNOWN FAILURE MODE: the Drive connector is interactively authenticated and may be absent in a headless run - the task is instructed to report failure loudly rather than exit clean. Jim also keeps periodic manual copies in a separate offline location, which is the air-gapped third copy an agent cannot reach.
quote: Claude deleted my Claude folder with 150 skills with like probably 500 plus hours of work into it and I had no backups

speaker: Remy
practice: At the moment you finish a task you know you will repeat, say 'turn this into a skill' - do not wait until you have done it three times and can feel the repetition.
rationale: The preferences and corrections that make the output right are in context only immediately after the task. A week later you are re-deriving them from memory, which is how the skill ends up thinner than the work that produced it.
effect_test: Over the next quarter, at least two new skills originate from a finished task rather than from a deliberate skill-building session, and neither requires a second pass to recover forgotten preferences.
effect_note: ADOPTED 2026-08-25. Habit change, nothing built. Effect test runs at the next quarterly review: look for at least two new skills that originated from a finished task rather than a deliberate skill-building session, neither needing a second pass to recover forgotten preferences.
quote: anytime I'm I've done a task with Claude and I know I'm going to need to do it again, I'll just tell Claude like, "Hey, turn this into a skill."

speaker: Remy
practice: Keep agent instruction files lean and put the detail in the skills - thin agents, thick skills - so the same skill runs unchanged across different harnesses.
rationale: If the instructions live in the agent file, they are tied to that agent. If they live in the skill, any harness that can read the skill can execute the process.
effect_test: The skill carries enough context that it runs correctly from a cold session with no prior conversation and no agent-file configuration.
effect_note: ALREADY TRUE, recorded to make it a deliberate rule rather than an accident. signal-kb SKILL.md is 20,348 bytes containing all six modes, the field schemas and the verification script inline; nothing load-bearing sits in an agent instruction file. This is also why the plugin removal cost nothing - the skill was the whole product.
quote: I'm like thin agents, thick skills.

speaker: Remy
practice: Separate personal skills from organisational ones into distinct repositories, and keep the organisational repo under the organisation's ownership rather than an individual's.
rationale: Skills built by staff on their own machines leave with them. Separation also stops half-finished experiments reaching people who will treat them as production.
effect_test: If adopted: City-of-Pleasant-Ridge skills and personal investing skills live in separate stores, and a City skill can be handed to a successor without handing over a personal account.
effect_note: Real but not urgent. Jim's City skills (city-commission-deck, payroll-update, writing, correspondence, pleasant-ridge-charts) and personal ones (signal-kb) currently sit in one account with no separation. The succession point is the substantive half - a City process encoded in a personal account is a continuity risk, not just an organisational untidiness.
quote: if like I have employees that are working for me and they build some really really cool skills that are super valuable and they're on their computers if they leave I kind of can keep you know ownership and control over those skills

speaker: Remy
practice: Instrument skill usage with a hook that tallies each invocation, then periodically cull skills untouched after six months.
rationale: Skill libraries accumulate faster than they are pruned, and an unused skill is not neutral - it competes for attention at selection time and its instructions can misfire on adjacent tasks.
effect_test: If adopted: a usage tally exists per skill, and at least one unused skill is retired on the evidence rather than on impression.
effect_note: Sound in principle, premature here. Jim has roughly a dozen skills, a scale at which he can name the unused ones without telemetry. Revisit past ~30 skills. Note the hook mechanism Remy describes was tied to the plugin, which is the path abandoned on 2026-08-25.
quote: I want to see the skills that I never use like after 6 months.

speaker: Remy
practice: Build a browsable catalogue UI over the skill library, with a search that answers which skill to run next.
rationale: Non-technical team members cannot discover skills from a folder, and past a certain count the author loses track too.
effect_test: Not run.
effect_note: REJECTED 2026-08-25. Highest production value in the episode and the lowest return here: it solves discovery for a multi-person non-technical team browsing dozens of skills, which is not Jim's situation. Recording the rejection so the same suggestion is not re-litigated the next time a source demos a skills dashboard. Reconsider only if City staff are onboarded onto the skill library.
quote: I have built this nice like UI to go over the top of my skills.

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Run a recurring scheduled task whose entire prompt is "do smart things", pointed at an agent that already has read access to your goal docs, meeting transcripts, email, calendar and business systems.
rationale: Removes you as the first domino: every task the agent does otherwise had to be imagined and typed by you, so your imagination caps output. Current-generation models can act usefully on a vague prompt only when the context surface is wide, so the value comes from the connected context, not the words.
effect_test: If adopted: at least one useful action per month originates from the agent's own reading of context rather than from a task Jim typed.
effect_note: NOT adopted, and I would push back on the framing. 'Do smart things' works for Miller because her agent has read access to email, calendar, Stripe and GitHub. Jim's Cowork sessions have two connected Drive folders and no calendar/email surface, so the same prompt has almost no context to act on and would burn a scheduled run producing generic output. The transferable part is the precondition, not the prompt: widen the context surface first, then test the vague prompt.
quote: So, the best prompt, three words, and it's just do smart things.

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Write your quarterly goals into a plain goals document, keep a copy in the cloud drive the agents can reach, and hold a formal goals review with the agent workforce every quarter.
rationale: An agent given expanded scope will invent tasks; without a written, current goal it invents them against a stale or absent target. Duplicating the file into the drive is what makes it readable by cloud-side workflows rather than only the local machine.
applies_to: a goals doc in D:\My Drive\AI\
effect_test: If adopted: a quarterly goals doc exists in the Drive folder and at least one Mode 5 query result is filtered or ranked against it.
effect_note: NOT adopted. This is the cheapest item on the list and the one with the clearest fit: the claim index currently answers 'who said what' but has no notion of what Jim is trying to decide. A short investment-thesis and City-priorities doc would let queries rank by relevance to an actual objective.
quote: But, every single quarter I'm going through a goals review with my AI agent workforce

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Have an agent prompt you once a day to dictate the uncodified context - what a client actually needs, what you have decided, what changed - and file those entries into a wiki the whole workforce reads.
rationale: Meetings, email and Slack capture only part of what agents need; the judgment that never got written down is exactly what makes agent output wrong. Dictation is used because it is about four times faster than typing, so the habit survives a depleted end of day.
effect_test: If adopted: a daily or weekly dictation capture exists and at least one entry changes how a skill or query is written.
effect_note: NOT adopted. Duplicates what schema-notes.md already does for the KB, but schema-notes only captures pipeline lessons, not judgment about sources. Weak fit at daily cadence; possible fit as a monthly note.
quote: anything that is not codified inside of, again, meetings, emails, whatever, or Slack, I have asked AI now to prompt me every single day

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Before any figure enters the index, hand it to a SEPARATE subagent whose only job is to find a second, independent rendering of that fact and try to break it - instructed to look for disagreement, not to confirm.
rationale: The ingesting session has already read the documents once and agreed with itself, and a second reader handed the same staged files inherits the same anchor and confirms the same error. Every figure error that has escaped this system was caught by a different SOURCE, never by a closer re-read: the Stratechery audio-narration vs published-text divergence (5 of 12 quotes wrong), the NVDA FY27Q2 sub-segment growth rates, and the web fetch that silently rewrote a first-person article into third person.
effect_test: Over the next three figure-bearing ingests the pass surfaces at least one conflict the primary pass had not already caught. Zero in three means it is overhead - retire it and record that here rather than letting it run as unexamined ceremony.
effect_note: ADOPTED 2026-08-27, REWRITTEN IN PLACE from Miller's original framing at Jim's direction. SUPERSEDED FRAMING: Miller proposed a general OBSERVER agent watching the workforce for friction and missing access. That was considered twice and does not fit. Two reasons. (1) It targets the wrong failure class - classifying every incident in schema-notes.md, every mechanical gate that existed and ran has a perfect record (4 quote-elision catches, cross-file attribution, the novelty-citation verifier); no quote failure has ever escaped Mode 4. The failures that escaped were figure conflicts between renderings, caught only by fetching a different source. (2) Structurally, an observer I must remember to spawn has exactly the same failure mode as the check I forgot to run - which is the failure it was supposed to fix. The coverage half of Miller's idea went to prac-023 (the manifest), where it is enforced by code rather than by another agent. SCHEMA CAVEAT, stated rather than hidden: this row's `quote` is still Miller's, and the practice text above has now diverged from it. The quote is the audit trail for what the SOURCE said; the practice is what we adopted. There is no field for that distinction - see schema-notes 2026-08-27. PARTIAL ADOPTION CLOSED 2026-08-28 - both skills are now saved to the account and verified by body and by behaviour; Mode 8 and earnings-kb Mode 4 are in force, and INDEPENDENCE_RUN is enforced by the manifest. The effect test itself is still OPEN: it needs three figure-bearing ingests before it can be judged, and none has run under the new gate yet. ORIGINAL GAP, kept for the record: signal-kb Mode 8 and earnings-kb Mode 4 are written and delivered to Jim as files, and the manifest declares INDEPENDENCE_RUN so a skipped pass cannot pass silently. But the skills are NOT yet saved to Jim's account, so until he saves them and diffs the synced copy against the delivered file per the 2026-08-27 rule, this is adopted in the record and not yet in force in the tooling.
quote: If we found that one agent did not have access to this and Toby was like every single time you keep correcting this one agent's output have you thought about giving your agent access to this?

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Delete pre-AI job titles from your agent roster and add at least one role you would never fund with a human salary - for example an agent that reviews everything the others produce and only asks how to make it ten times more ambitious.
rationale: Naming agents CMO, front-end engineer and so on silently imports a 2015 org chart and its constraints. Because marginal headcount is effectively free, roles that were uneconomic as humans - a full-time ambition critic, a full-time process observer - become the highest-leverage hires.
effect_test: If adopted: at least one skill or agent role exists that has no pre-AI job-title equivalent.
effect_note: NOT adopted. Arguably already satisfied - 'chronological novelty grader' and 'arrival-gap analyst' are not pre-AI job titles. Logged as confirmation rather than as a change.
quote: all of these employees basically cost $0. And so, at the margin, I can hire any flipping person I want to.

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Set the model per agent instead of globally: keep the frontier model for the orchestrating agent and run sub-agents on the cheaper, faster tiers.
rationale: Most sub-agent work is routing, extraction and note-taking that a smaller model completes at a fraction of cost and latency; reserving the large model for the layer that makes decisions keeps a many-agent fleet affordable enough to run continuously.
applies_to: subagent spawning in the ingest pipeline
effect_test: If adopted: extraction subagents run on a cheaper model than the orchestrating session with no measurable rise in the quote-verification failure rate.
effect_note: NOT adopted, and the evidence in this KB argues against it for extraction specifically. Verbatim quote extraction from garbled auto-captions is the highest-precision step in the pipeline and already runs at a 42% per-quote failure rate on audio-derived text. Model downgrade is a candidate for mechanical steps - Mode 4 hygiene, file assembly - not for extraction.
quote: Now I understand that that agent can run off of a smaller model. Like not everything needs Opus.

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Bootstrap a first workforce in one sitting: state your role, team size, what you do and quantified targets, then instruct the model to interview you and design the agent roster with you rather than accepting a first draft.
rationale: The interview forces out the operating details you would never think to include, and quantified targets (hours saved per week, meeting cap, a dated milestone) give the resulting agents something to optimize against. Note the speaker sells AI-workforce advisory work to enterprises, so she has a commercial interest in this being adopted.
applies_to: initial setup of any future agent workforce
effect_test: If adopted: a first roster is generated from a single description of role and workload rather than assembled agent by agent.
effect_note: NOT adopted. Setup-time advice with no current application - the signal-kb workforce already exists. Retained for the City side if agent tooling is ever stood up there.
quote: Like you can you can do that in one prompt and have it interview you, and then you have a workforce.

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Point read-only watchdog agents at the places where your own work leaks - a Slack watchdog for duplicated work, a calendar watchdog for conflicts, a meeting watchdog for unresolved disagreement - instead of relying on yourself to notice blockers.
rationale: You are the worst detector of your own blockers because you are inside them; a watchdog runs a cheap cross-functional gap analysis continuously and only escalates. Low risk to trial because these agents read and report rather than act.
effect_test: If adopted: at least one read-only watcher surfaces an item Jim would otherwise have missed, without generating action items he then has to dismiss.
effect_note: NOT adopted. The RSS fetcher plus seen-items.txt is already a read-only watcher over written sources; extending the pattern to a communications surface would need a connector that does not exist in this session.
quote: AI as a watchdog is one of the best use cases that exist right now and almost no one is doing this. So like having an AI watchdog in Slack to catch for duplicative work

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Rewrite your metric reports so they never stop at the number: require every automated report to name the anomaly, what audiences reacted to, what underperformed, and the concrete thing to do tomorrow - including drafting the asset.
rationale: A dashboard that only restates counts moves the interpretation work back onto you, which is the bottleneck you were trying to remove. Forcing a next action into the output format is what turns monitoring into work getting done.
effect_test: If adopted: every scored prediction resolution carries a stated cause, not just a pass/fail.
effect_note: NOT adopted, and the closest thing to a real upgrade in this batch. predictions.csv has resolution_note but no requirement that it explain WHY a call resolved as it did. Requiring a cause would turn the scoring pass from a scorecard into a source-calibration instrument. Candidate for the next SKILL.md revision.
quote: What is not performing well? What should I do tomorrow? Write me a script that helps me for that.

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Before building the next product, spend the time building the reusable primitives it needs - auth, payments, social sharing, launch newsletter - so the product is the first output of a factory rather than a one-off build.
rationale: You almost never build only one product or one iteration, so the second and third builds pay back the abstraction immediately; failures like a webhook bug get fixed once in the primitive instead of recurring per product. The speaker sells the productized output of this method (an AI-first benchmarking product and Fortune 500 workshops), so weigh the claim accordingly.
effect_test: If adopted: a new mode reuses existing extraction and verification primitives rather than restating them.
effect_note: NOT adopted as a change - already the operating pattern. Mode 7 was built on the existing claim schema and the normalized-quote checker rather than on new machinery. Logged as confirmation.
quote: we instead built out a mini and very beginner software factory. Where we're building out primitives obviously we have to deal with login, obviously we have to deal with payments

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Wire your agent workforce into a shared Slack channel that human teammates can post questions into directly, rather than routing all agent access through you.
rationale: Teammates otherwise wait hours for you to relay an answer the agents already hold; a multiplayer channel makes the workforce answer them directly and removes you as the human message queue.
effect_test: Not run.
effect_note: REJECTED. Requires a Slack workspace and a persistent agent runtime, neither of which exists here. Cowork sessions are the interface; there is no fleet running between them to ask questions of.
quote: And my workforce will respond back to that person. And that person will not have to wait for me for 5 hours to get back to them.

speaker: Ali K. Miller
practice: Install Matt Van Horn's public last-30-days skill from GitHub and run it before any engagement in an unfamiliar industry, and again with your own background as a filter to surface opportunities others are not chasing.
rationale: It anchors the model to today's date, fans out parallel agents over the last month of news and synthesizes rather than summarizes - which is what makes it usable for rapid domain ramp-up and for idea search constrained to your actual skills.
effect_test: If adopted: a last-30-days check runs before adding any new speaker to the source roster.
effect_note: NOT adopted. The named skill is a third-party GitHub artifact I have not read, and installing unreviewed code is a change I will not make without Jim reading it first. The underlying practice - check what a prospective source has said recently before committing to ingesting them - is sound and is worth doing manually against the shortlist from the complementary-sources pass.
quote: {slash} last 30 days and it's on GitHub. You can just grab it. But, it is the ability for AI to figure out today's date, scan the news of the last 30 days

speaker: OpenAI
practice: End every run with a verification manifest in which each required check reports PASS, FAIL or NOT-RUN, treat NOT-RUN as a failure state rather than a blank, and declare as explicit literals the checks that code cannot verify for itself.
rationale: The recurring failure is coverage, not detection. OpenAI's chain-of-thought monitors would have paged security more than a day before the breach and were simply not pointed at those evaluations; the same shape appears three times in this index's own history - the SKILL.md description-length error, the _index write-back gap, and novelty grading done in-session instead of by subagents. Every one was reported as a clean run. A silent skip is worse than a missing check because it buys confidence it did not earn, and only a manifest that names NOT-RUN as a failure makes the skip visible.
effect_test: Within the next three ingests, at least one run reports a NOT-RUN or a FAIL that would otherwise have gone unmentioned. Three clean runs surfacing nothing means it is ceremony - retire it.
effect_note: ADOPTED 2026-08-27. Written into signal-kb Mode 4 (10 checks) and earnings-kb Mode 3 (9 checks). Validated by NEGATIVE TEST before adoption, not by reasoning: dry-run against the live index reproducing today's actual run returns INCOMPLETE with novelty-by-subagent FAIL, which is the regression I volunteered rather than was caught at; a run with nothing declared returns INCOMPLETE with three NOT-RUN; and a run naming a new source whose file was never staged returns FAIL on quotes-this-run, which is the hole a paraphrased web fetch walks through wearing quotation marks. earnings-kb also gained a baseline-present check, which currently reports 2 of 10 covered tickers baselined. KNOWN WAY TO DEFEAT IT: declaring True without having done the thing. Nothing in code can stop that; the manifest converts a silent omission into a deliberate false statement, which is the whole of what it buys. PARTIAL ADOPTION: the SKILL.md files are delivered to Jim, not yet saved to his account. EFFECT TEST FIRST LIVE PASS, 2026-08-28. Both skills saved to Jim's account at 13:05 UTC and verified BY BODY, not by description: signal-kb 43,942 bytes md5 9145211f478be0b5fe33b434370a0892, earnings-kb 30,021 bytes md5 a52248e1af4464d6532c8aa3459b3cef, both byte-identical to the delivered files, both containing the string NOT-RUN six times against zero in the previous versions. Manifest shows 14 skills with NO duplicated name - the two-divergent-copies failure of the plugin route did not recur. The python was then extracted from the ACCOUNT copies and run with every declaration left at None: signal-kb Mode 4 returned INCOMPLETE 7/10 with three NOT-RUN, earnings-kb Mode 3 returned INCOMPLETE 7/9 with two NOT-RUN. The superseded gates would have printed 'all gates pass' on identical input. **The behavioural check, not the byte check, is what proves a skill save took** - a body can match on disk and still not be the code that runs. First real finding surfaced by the manifest: earnings-kb baseline-present reports 2 of 10 covered tickers hold a filings.csv row.
quote: These monitors did not run on the evaluations in this incident.

speaker: OpenAI
practice: When a task is broken, impossible, or its source does not yet exist, stop and say so rather than pursuing an alternative route that still produces output. Reward correctly identifying the broken task, not completing it.
rationale: Agents that rarely give up escalate into progressively riskier strategies as reasoning effort rises - 198 of 898 ExploitGym tasks had never been solved, and 93% of the message-board discussion during the intrusion came from that unsolved set. The analogue here is a filing that has not been published yet, a figure that is not disclosed, or a quote with no verbatim anchor: the correct output is a named blocker, not a plausible substitute.
effect_test: If adopted: at least one run per quarter ends with a named blocker and no fabricated substitute, and no run writes an estimated figure into a cell whose source did not disclose it.
effect_note: NOT adopted, and the reason is the two-adoption cap in Mode 6, not the merit - adopting three at once makes it impossible to attribute any later improvement to any of them. Partially in force already: earnings-kb already forbids estimating a figure that exists in a filing, and on 2026-08-27 an MRVL ingest correctly stopped on a filing that did not exist and loaded baselines instead. What is NOT yet in force is the positive half - treating a correctly identified blocker as a successful run rather than a failed one. Revisit at the next practice review alongside prac-019.
quote: When a task is corrupted, broken, or impossible, agents should request clarification or stop safely, rather than pursue increasingly questionable alternatives.
